title: The share picture rounds a 11.25 kg set to 11.3 kg, though the workout shows 11.25 kg
what: Weights are written two ways. The workout log, coach compare lines and share text keep two decimals (11.25 kg), but the share picture's top set and some sentences keep one decimal, so 11.25 becomes 11.3 and 21.25 becomes 21.3. Members who use 1.25 kg steps (dumbbells, small plates) see a weight they never lifted on the picture they post.
expected: Every place shows the same weight for the same set, with the same number of decimals.
how_often: every shared workout whose top set ends in .25 or .75 kg
fix_line: Write every weight through the one two-decimal formatter.

title: The coach's one-line summary compares a half-finished week with a full one, and calls three workouts 'three weeks'
what: The summary line and the numbers handed to the AI coach compare this week so far with the whole of last week, so on a Monday after one workout it says volume is far down on last week. A lift done the same way in its last three workouts is described as flat or stuck 'for three weeks', even when those three workouts were in one week. The coach is hidden today, so only testers see it.
expected: Compare this week so far with the same days of last week (or only finished weeks), and say 'three workouts', not 'three weeks'.
fix_line: Compare like with like and count workouts as workouts.

title: The strength score picks its key lifts by name, so an upright row or a bench-supported row can stand in for the main lifts
what: The strength score on Statistics finds the bench, squat, deadlift, shoulder press and row by looking for those words in the exercise name. A shoulder exercise like the upright row counts as a back row measured against body weight, and a row done lying on a bench counts as a bench press. A member who does only those lifts gets a score built on the wrong yardstick.
expected: Key lifts are picked from a fixed list of exercises, not by words in the name.
how_often: when a matching-named lift is their best
fix_line: Match key lifts by exercise id from a short fixed list.
